944.author: zhaozhaozz
944.body:
Nightly and release real E2E runs showed only a gate line, so a reader could not see how each selected case finished. This publishes one per-case execution table for `profile: daily` and `profile: release`. Merge and pull-request profiles do not publish it. The slice summary, the non-gating PUCT review table, and the Biomni suite report stay as they are.

## Case execution table

The combined real E2E accounting job writes the table into its job summary, into the run artifact `case-execution-details.md`, and into the existing `real-e2e-results` artifact as `dashboard-summary.json`. Nightly appends that same Markdown to the outcome summary next to the existing gate line. A release run uses the same real E2E workflow, so its accounting summary and artifact carry the table too.

Columns, in order: `#`, `case`, `status`, `score`, `peak memory GB`, `generated tokens`, `judge tokens`, `total tokens`, `tool calls`, `duration min`.

`#` starts at 1. Rows with `started_at` come first, oldest first. Selected cases with no `started_at` follow, ordered by case id. Every selected case is one row, including failed and unfinished cases.

`score` uses `evaluation.overall_score`, then `evaluation.total_score`, then `evaluation.score`. It does not use the non-gating PUCT review score or `evaluation.race.overall_score`. `duration min` is `generation_duration_ms / 60000`, to one decimal place. Generated tokens are the generator's recorded completion tokens. When a usage record has only a total, that total is shown and the split is `n/a`. Token counts of at least 1000 use a compact form (`34.2K`, `14.5M`); smaller counts stay integers. A missing measurement is the text `n/a`. A recorded zero stays zero. A missing optional cell does not change the gate verdict. The required check name `merge-gate` and the ruleset are unchanged.

The table and `dashboard-summary.json` copy only these identity and numeric cells. Prompts, answers, traces, assertion text, error strings, and secrets are not copied.

`dashboard-summary.json` keeps the existing count fields (`tests`, `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `flaky`, with the last four summing to `tests`) and may add an optional `table`. The producer writes the final display strings, including `n/a` and compact token counts. A summary without `table` remains counts-only. Any consumer that already reads `dashboard-summary.json` from a test-results artifact can render `table` from the declared columns, without a repository-specific parser.

## Validation

On `27ae924c95f4a4a8867b78915fb8e8ec391f05cc`:

- `node --test .ci/case-execution.test.mjs`: 5 passed, 0 failed. This covers the header and column order, `started_at` ordering, `n/a` for a missing metric, inclusion of a failed case and an unfinished case, score precedence, and exclusion of a planted secret and model text from the Markdown and the summary. It also checks that `merge` and `pr` write neither file, and that the workflow steps run only for `daily` and `release`.
- `pnpm ci:selftest`: 123 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4, failed 0, skipped 0.
- `pnpm docs:check`: passed, 0 lint problems.

The self-test, L1, and docs check ran on this commit before it was pushed. This review re-ran the case-execution contract test on the same commit. No paid real-model daily or release run was dispatched, so this pull request does not yet include a live GitHub Actions log of the new table.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. This change only publishes CI evidence: a job summary, a Markdown artifact, and fields inside `dashboard-summary.json`. It does not change a product page, API, CLI, runner, or which cases execute, and it adds no user-visible product path. The contract test above is the check for the new table.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: none for product users. Nightly and release run summaries gain a per-case execution table.

Compatibility and migration: none. `merge-gate` is unchanged. Summaries that omit `table` parse as they do today.

Fixes #850

950.body:
The title over the conversation is printed from the open Session's own
record, while the sidebar already followed a rename the moment it happened. A
Session's first message is named by the service ahead of the run, on the stream
the app is already reading, so the row appeared with the message and the bar
kept saying 未命名会话 for as long as the answer streamed. Renaming from the
row's menu or from the bar itself had the same lag: the write reached the list,
and the bar kept the old name until the Session was reopened.

Fixes #957.

## Take the name from the evidence already in hand

`session.updated` carries the renamed Session, and the rename route's reply
carries it too. Both are merged into the open `detail`, so the bar and the row
print the same name at the same moment. Messages are preserved by the merge,
and no extra request is made: the event is the service saying the title
changed, which arrives end-to-end earlier than the read-back that follows the
run.

## Never fold a replayed record over a newer one

The stream a run is followed on replays from cursor 0, so opening a Session
whose run is still going delivers its earlier `session.updated` again — older
than the record `openSession` has just read. Folding it would put the bar back
under the name from before the user's own rename, and the composer back under
the approval mode and the expert it had then, until the run ended: the same
bar/row disagreement this PR removes, reached by leaving the Session and coming
back.

Every write on the service stamps `updatedAt` (`store.updateSession`,
`compareAndSetSessionTitle`, the approval-mode and expert writes), so the merge
now takes the newer record whatever order the two arrive in
(`apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts:983`). A record of the same age is the
same state and may land. The merge also lands in the cache that paints a
Session on the way back to it, so the older title is not shown while the read
is in flight.

The regression journey seeds exactly that: a live run whose log holds the
record written before the rename, a rename from the bar, a switch to another
Session and back. Held open until the page is being looked at, the replay has
provably reached it when the assertions run.

## Screenshots

Before is the merge base `face1d40`; after is this branch. Both are the same
mocked workspace running the same journey — the bar over the conversation and
the sidebar row that must agree with it.

**Rename from the bar — zh-CN**

In the "before" images the sidebar row already carries the new name while the
bar over the conversation still prints the old one (`晶体结构分析` /
`Untitled session`) — the defect. The run's read-back is held open for the
seconds the capture takes, which is the window the defect lived in.

## Test entry: hold one route's answer

The mock that answers `/api/**` for the desktop browser entry can hold a
matching route's answer until the spec releases it. That is what lets the new
journeys look at the bar while the run's read-back is still outstanding — the
window the defect lived in, and one that no assertion on final state can see.

It also answers the run-events route as a stream to a caller that subscribes
(`accept: text/event-stream`) and as JSON to the one rebuilding a finished run,
because the replay that the second new journey is about only happens on the
subscribed path.

## Validation

Baseline `7057aaf6`: the two original assertions fail with the old name still
in the bar (`晶体结构分析` and `未命名会话`). With the freshness gate removed
from this branch, the third journey fails the same way at
`sessions.spec.ts:246`, so it pins the replayed-record case rather than
passing for its own reasons.

- Desktop browser E2E (L2 mocked entry, `apps/desktop/e2e`): 105 passed /

- `pnpm typecheck` (desktop): exit 0.
- CI run `42183005892` on this head: policy, L1, UT, ST, Coverage,
  merge-gate and all five mocked E2E shards pass. The run before it failed ST

  `services/api/src/configuration/p1-runtime.integration.test.ts`
  (`model.repair_credential`, `Run not found`); that file passes 12/12 on this

Earlier heads on this branch ran the same layers: L1 4/4, UT 6403/6390 passed
with 13 failures, ST 50/51, mocked browser E2E 126/133. The 13 UT and 1 ST
failures reproduce unchanged on an unmodified worktree of `main` and are
host-side:

- `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` — this host's bubblewrap 0.6.1
  has no `--disable-userns`.
- `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` (5) and
  `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts` (5) — the owned services these
  tests start exit before becoming healthy here.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` — the recorded
  trajectory of a JiuwenSwarm turn.
- `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs` — the harness' own pre-fix body restored
  anyway.
- `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` (ST) — the pinned Python runtime comes
  from GitHub Releases and exceeds that journey's five-minute download budget
  from this host.

The 7 mocked E2E failures on the earlier head were all `apps/web` journeys;
three reproduce identically on unmodified `main` (two font-metric layout
ceilings on this host, and one blocked on a micromamba download), and the other
four pass on both trees when re-run. This diff touches only `apps/desktop`.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — tested SHA `4b11b27f`. Browser, desktop L2 mocked entry:

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rename a Session from the bar (double-click the title) | Row and bar both show the new name at once; the write survives a reload | PASS |
| Send the first message in a new Session while the run's read-back is held open | Row and bar both show the name the service published ahead of the run; 未命名会话 does not linger | PASS |
| Rename, switch to another Session and back while a run is going, then release the run's replay | The replayed `session.updated` arrives and changes neither the name in the bar nor the composer's permission mode | PASS |

Command: `playwright test --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts`
(105 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped).

The desktop L2 entry mocks every `/api/**` response; the real-stack journey
(`apps/desktop/e2e-real`, tier L3) is unchanged by this front-end state fix and
was not part of this verification.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: the conversation's title updates at the same moment as its
sidebar row, including the automatic name taken from a first message, and a
return to a Session that is still running no longer shows the name it had
before it was renamed.
Compatibility and migration: none.

The `release:fix` label cannot be applied from this fork (the account has no
write access to the upstream repository); the label is pending a maintainer.

959.body:
## What this fixes

Two `settle`s can overlap. `send` clears `running` **before** it awaits `settle` (`use-workspace.ts:1141-1144`), so the composer is usable again while a settle's three reads — `getSession` → `listRuns` → `buildReplays` (which may re-read run events one by one) — are still in flight. The next message's turn can then end and start a second settle before the first one lands.

The older settle wrote its stale snapshot unconditionally:

- `commitReplays(target, batch)` replaced the session's replay cache with an older, shorter list. Its internal `replayEpoch` is only bumped by `clearSession`, not per settle.
- `rememberBounded(detailsBySession, target, fresh)` replaced the first-screen cache with the older transcript.
- `setDetail(fresh)` put the older transcript on screen, hiding the newer message and its answer until the next turn — and moving the design anchor back to the previous design, which reopens the auto-continue stall path fixed by F9/F12.

Reproduction: send a message in a long session (slow `getSession`) or the first turn after a refresh (`buildReplays` re-reading run events), and have the next message's stream fail/end quickly. The second settle lands first, the first lands last.

## The fix

`apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts`, two changes:

1. New `settleEpoch`, incremented by every `settle`. Each settle asks at each write whether it is still the newest one (`newest()`), so the decision is made when the write happens, not when the reads started. The three writes above are gated by it. `sendEpoch` continues to guard the pending message and `resetRun`; `refreshSessionLists` / `refreshPanel` stay unconditional because a stale settle's refresh is still a refresh.
2. `clearSession` bumps `settleEpoch` as well. `openSession` calls `clearSession()` and then sets `sessionRef`; leaving A and reopening A before an A-settle lands would otherwise make that settle look current again even though its reads describe the left Session. This mirrors the existing `replayEpoch` handling.

No changes to `follow`, `openSession`, `buildReplays`, or `replayEpoch`'s existing uses.

## Test

New `apps/desktop/tests/workspace-settle-order.test.ts` (sibling of `workspace-settle.test.ts`, same harness): both turns end at once, so both sends start a settle; the newer settle lands first with `[FIRST, SECOND, ANSWER]`, then the older one lands with `[FIRST]`. The assertion is that the transcript stays `[FIRST, SECOND, ANSWER]`.

Red first, on the unmodified source:

```
not ok 1 - a settle that lands after a newer one does not put its older transcript back
  error: |-
    the older settle did not write
    + actual - expected

      [
        '/evolve-design --algorithm puct 一',
    -   '/evolve-design --algorithm puct 二',
    -   'answer 2'
      ]
```

Green after the fix:

```
$ npx tsx --test tests/workspace-settle-order.test.ts
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

Full suite and typecheck in `apps/desktop` with the fix:

```
$ npm test
# tests 821
# pass 821
# fail 0

$ npm run typecheck
(clean)
```

## Relation to #814

This is the last finding (F13) from the #814 review, where it was confirmed but left out of that PR so its approvals would not be invalidated. **#814 is not touched** (it has since merged); this PR is based on `main`.

Not merged manually — CI + committer approval as usual.

960.author: yuanzhou75
960.body:
Fixes #952

## Why

`spawn python ENOENT` did not come from JiuwenSwarm: it came from the API's own stdio MCP client. `extensions_config.json` declares one stdio server `biomed` (`python -m sciencediscovery_gateway.public_biomed_mcp`), and every literature connector (arxiv, pubmed, europe-pmc, biorxiv, medrxiv) is bound to it, so one failed spawn removed all five.

`resolveMcpPython()` was supposed to find the venv `scripts/start-stack.sh` provisions, but it only probed paths relative to the process cwd (`data/envs/gateway`, `services/gateway/.venv`) and then returned a bare `"python"`. The reporter's stack is `cd ~/sd779 && node services/api/dist/server.js` with `SCIENCE_AGENT_GATEWAY_PYTHON_PATH` unset — exactly the case where the venv at `<data dir>/envs/gateway` exists (`.env.example` promises it) but was never probed, while the host has only `/usr/bin/python3`. The model then saw the connectors as unavailable.

The Issue's original remedies (a `python` → `python3` symlink, `command: "python3"`, a `python3` fallback) would not have restored retrieval: `python` and `python3` go through the same resolver, and a system `python3` cannot import `sciencediscovery_gateway`.

## What changed

- `resolveMcpPython(env, dataDir?)` now probes the venvs this repository provisions under the API's real data dir, in priority order:
  1. `SCIENCE_AGENT_GATEWAY_PYTHON_PATH` (still authoritative)
  2. `<data dir>/envs/gateway` (`scripts/start-stack.sh`)
  3. `<data dir>/envs/sd-services` (`scripts/start-stack.mjs` and packaged installs)
  4. `$SCIENCE_AGENT_ENVS_ROOT` (Docker)
  5. the legacy `data/envs/gateway` and `services/gateway/.venv` layouts
  6. a `python` already on PATH, resolved to its absolute path
- When none of those is runnable, the resolver fails fast with the operator's remedy (set `SCIENCE_AGENT_GATEWAY_PYTHON_PATH`, or provision/start through `scripts/start-stack.sh`) and the probed paths, instead of returning a bare `python` that can only fail later with `ENOENT`.
- `McpNodeClient` takes the data dir (`new McpNodeClient(..., { dataDir: config.dataDir })` in `bootstrap/platform.ts`) and records the interpreter it resolved on `mcp_connection_started` / `_failed` / `_succeeded` (`python: <path>`, `python: unresolved` plus the reason), so this failure is self-diagnosing in `<data dir>/logs/api.log` rather than only visible in a subagent artifact.
- venv interpreters are matched in both `bin/python` and `Scripts/python.exe`, and only regular executable files are accepted.
- `.env.example` now documents the resolution order and the fail-fast.

## Verification

Regression tests in `services/api/src/mcp/node-client.test.ts` (written against a temporary data dir, so they do not depend on the host PATH):

- the provisioned `<data dir>/envs/gateway` venv is found with no environment hint, as is `envs/sd-services` and `$SCIENCE_AGENT_ENVS_ROOT`
- an operator `SCIENCE_AGENT_GATEWAY_PYTHON_PATH` still wins over a provisioned venv
- the default `.sciencediscovery-data` and the legacy `data/` layouts are still resolved from the process cwd
- a `python` on PATH resolves to its absolute path; with nothing at all the resolver throws the remediation message
- a bundled `python` server logs the resolved interpreter, and logs `unresolved` plus the reason when resolution fails

Local: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` clean; `node --import tsx --test src/mcp/node-client.test.ts` 24/24 pass.

## Notes for review

- The explicit `SCIENCE_AGENT_GATEWAY_PYTHON_PATH` is unchanged, so every launcher (`start-stack.sh`, `start-stack.mjs`, `serve.ts`, Docker) keeps today's behaviour; only the fallback and its failure mode change.

963.author: zhaozhaozz
963.body:
The daily and release case table was leaving judge tokens, tool calls, and most session token cells as n/a even when the run had already recorded them. The table reads the staged projection, and that projection keeps only the numbers `executionMeasurements` returns. DeepResearchBench stores each judge call under `evaluation.judge_calls`, and staging then dropped that ledger, so the judge-token column stayed empty. Journeys other than Biomni never recorded a tool-call count at all.

Judge tokens now fall back, after the existing measured sources, to the sum of `evaluation.judge_calls[].usage.total_tokens`. Every recorded call must be a non-negative safe integer. One missing value, or an empty list, leaves the cell empty. There is no partial sum and no invented 0. A value the case already stored in `measurements.judge_tokens` still wins.

Real cases that have a Session collect shared measurements before cleanup, from the same public session API the Web client uses:

- Generated tokens and total tokens come from `GET /api/sessions/:id/usage`, one invocation at a time. If any invocation is not reported, or any of input, output, or total is missing, both cells stay empty. The summary bucket skips unreported calls, so a document that already carries the raw invocation list now follows the same rule instead of publishing that partial bucket.
- Tool calls are distinct `trace.id` values on `tool.started` and `tool.completed`, plus `toolCallId` on tool steps in each subagent stream. PUCT also reads evolve run events. The same id counts once. Model invocation count is never used as a tool count. Every stream read and no tool call records 0. A missing stream, truncated history, a tool event without an id, or a catalog tool step that no stream recorded leaves the cell empty.
- Collection does not throw. It borrows 60 seconds and then returns that time plus the time it actually used, so it cannot turn a passing case into a failure or a failing case into a pass. Duration is still only `generation_duration_ms`. Nothing new is invented from the Playwright timeout.

DeepResearchBench, TC-E2E-01, and PUCT-COMPRESS keep their existing metrics document and only add these numbers. The basic, runner-recovery, inline-card, and J5 journeys write `case-metrics.json`, which contains the plan case id, the tagged key, and the numbers. The staging allowlist and the table's filename match include that name. Two metrics documents for one case still blank the row, so each case keeps one document.

Peak memory, the score column, and the merge gate are unchanged. The score is still only `evaluation.overall_score`, then `total_score`, then `score`. `evaluation.race.overall_score` is still not read. A missing measurement stays n/a and does not fail the case.

Replaying the raw DeepResearchBench metrics from Nightly run 42153537119 through this projection changes only four judge-token cells: DRB-58 739.6K, DRB-59 744.3K, DRB-64 185.1K, and DRB-75 146.6K. Those match the `judge_calls` sums from that run (739606, 744286, 185142, 146570). DRB-62 did not run its evaluation and stays n/a. Score, peak memory, the other cells, and the row counts stay as published. The projected file does not keep `judge_calls` or the prompt. Tool-call counts and the new `case-metrics.json` numbers are not in that old evidence; they show up on the next daily or release run. TC-E2E-01 and PUCT do not write `judge_calls`, so their judge-token cells stay n/a.

A provider-fault retry can already write a second metrics document in another instance directory, and the table then blanks that case. This change does not fix that. A retry of a journey that now writes `case-metrics.json` can blank the new row the same way, which leaves n/a rather than a wrong number.

Follow-up to #850. That issue stays closed.

## Validation

On `6072aee0392ed70873665efc085bec4fdcd65032`:

- `node --test .ci/case-execution.test.mjs`: 10 passed, 0 failed. The new cases cover a complete judge-call sum, a missing call, reported session usage, an unreported call, distinct tool ids, an empty tool stream as 0, a truncated or missing stream as n/a, `case-metrics.json` identity, a second document blanking the row, and a projection that publishes the judge total without the ledger.
- `node --import tsx --test test/helpers/case-measurements.unit.ts`: 2 passed, 0 failed. Collection does not throw, the borrowed timeout is returned, and `case-metrics.json` contains only the identity and the numbers.
- `node --test .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: 28 passed, 0 failed, including the new filename on the staging allowlist.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not re-run for this change. The author also reported `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs` at 128 passed / 0 failed, the tagged daily plan still listing the same 19 real cases, and release listing those 19 plus 50 Biomni L5 cases. This review did not repeat that broader suite or the Nightly artifact replay.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. There is no new product entry, API, CLI, or Runner behavior. Real cases write one extra numeric metrics document from session APIs that already exist, and a missing number does not change the journey result. No mocked browser journey and no paid real-model run was executed for this change. The pull-request checks still run the usual layers.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: none in the product. The next daily or release case table can show judge tokens, generated tokens, total tokens, and tool calls where the run recorded them. Missing values stay n/a.

Compatibility and migration: none.

The desktop app could turn scientific memory on, but there was nothing to do with it: a final report's `[evidence1]` and `[artifact1]` references rendered as literal brackets, and the graph had no surface a reader could reach from the report they were reading. This change makes those references citations the reader can follow, and keeps the one remaining memory surface — the switch — where the reader can act on it. ## A report's citations become chips The alias → node map is persisted on the report version (`references`), and the Markdown reader turns a token only when that map answers for it. `[note]`, an unknown alias, and every report written before the back-fill render as the plain text they are. The transform runs on the mdast tree rather than on rendered text: a chip is a link node carrying `graph://`, so it survives emphasis and line breaks inside a sentence, and the `a` renderer turns it into a button. `urlTransform` lets `graph://` through and still applies the default safety transform to every other URL. Chips travel with the run stream too. The server back-fills `references` onto the persisted message right before `run.completed`, so a live answer and its replay show the same chips instead of the replay falling back to text. ## An artifact citation opens the document, not a record about it An artifact chip opens `ArtifactDialog` over the report: the version the citation pins (not the newest one), with its own picker, and a 溯源 tab. An evidence chip opens the node's own fields — type, locator, confidence, source, recorded time — plus a 溯源 tab with the linear walk the graph recorded: the evidence, the paper or record it came from, the skill that read it, the session that ran it. Neither dialog is a library: closing it leaves the reader in the sentence they were reading. An 上游文件 link inside provenance opens the dependency in the panel beside the dialog instead of replacing the document under the cursor, and the dialog steps aside while the panel is showing it. Pointing the panel anywhere else ends that gesture, so the dialog never keeps an offset for a surface that no longer shows the dependency. ## Settings carries the switch and its state The header capsule polled `/api/health` on a timer whether or not memory was on. It is gone. Whether the service answers is now a line beside 启用科学记忆, read once when the switch turns on, and again only when the reader presses 重新检查. Where the graph is stored stays the memory service's own configuration — the page asks for nothing it does not show. 科学记忆 moves to 智能, after 专家. The line has two readings: 运行正常, or 连接失败. A store that has not been given its credential (a Neo4j deployment's own configuration) used to read 需要密码 here; that named a step no control in this window could take, so it now reads as any other service that is not working, and the state, label and style rule are gone. ## Reading a document twice is a render, not a second read Version bytes are cached module-side per version id, keyed by the client and session, with in-flight reads deduplicated and an LRU cap (24 MB total, 4 MB per entry) so a run of large documents cannot grow without bound. Reopening the artifact dialog, or opening a citation whose dependency is already on screen, issues no second request. The JSON and CSV previews parse once per content instead of once per paint, and `AssistantTurns` is memoised so opening a dialog does not re-parse every answer in the session. ## The memory sidecar can no longer take the stack down `scripts/start-stack.mjs` pins the sidecar's store under the app data directory (an explicit `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` still wins), derives its URL from the port this stack binds instead of inheriting a stale one, and degrades to `memoryGraph="degraded"` when the sidecar does not become healthy rather than aborting the whole start. Nothing is migrated automatically, and nothing needs to be: a report's `references` still name the same node ids, so pointing the variable back at the old store restores every existing citation as it was written. - **An unhealthy memory-graph no longer aborts the stack.** The `.mjs` stack warns, stops the child, and lets the API report `memoryGraph="degraded"` on `/api/health`, which is the state the settings line and the card already show; `start-stack.sh` still calls `wait_healthy` unguarded and aborts under `set -euo pipefail`. The divergence is deliberate — scientific memory is optional and the reader toggles it, and the bash entry point is left as-is for Linux/macOS and Docker users — and it is stated in the file's header. The URL follows the same rule: when this stack starts its own sidecar the API is pointed at the port it binds (an inherited `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_URL` is ignored with a warning), and when it starts none — `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_AVAILABLE=0`, or no Python — the operator's explicit URL is kept as-is. The chip URL gained a `?v=` suffix so two versions of one artifact stay distinct. It is built and parsed in memory only; no stored field, API response or persisted report carries it.

## Summary

Part of #835.

This is the independent tool-output trust-boundary slice from the staged landing plan. It introduces category-driven fencing for model-visible untrusted content while preserving raw stored evidence and observer behavior. It does not register Knowledge Engine tools or change kbScope, research state, finish-gate, or agent memory.

### Included

- Per-registry nonces and explicit `untrustedCategory` classification, with legacy-name and MCP-remote fallback behavior.
- Fencing for tool-domain, MCP, remote, and error payloads; only genuine framework-control messages bypass the boundary.
- Durable output sidecars preserving trust and neutralization metadata through line, character, and search readbacks. New records carry an explicit trust format version; pre-metadata records fail closed as untrusted legacy content, while authenticated fence metadata prevents planted fence-shaped tool text from changing durable status or evidence.
- Connector-controlled tool-search results are fenced and neutralized. Model-facing tool descriptions and schema `description`/`title`/`$comment` metadata receive the same protection without changing property identifiers, enum values, or the execution-time schema.
- A shared TypeScript/adapter/durable-store nonce, with native web and subagent history fenced at the actual model-request and dynamic-context rehydration boundaries. Existing fences are unwrapped during hydration only at a legacy anchored position or when framework metadata authenticates the category and nonce; missing trust wiring fails closed.
- Tool identity resolution through assistant `tool_call_id` mappings, including OpenAI tool messages without `name`; platform output is not double-fenced.
- Equivalent native-history handling for JiuwenSwarm housekeeping/default compression requests. Housekeeping selects a provider only when platform-call history proves one unique active run through its `_sd_run`; concurrent runs stay isolated, and finished, foreign, or ambiguous history fails closed instead of borrowing another run's model, credentials, or nonce.
- Framework truncation/readback/failure guidance kept outside untrusted fences, including explicit post-fence overflow notices and durable readback references.
- Final model-message fitting that enforces byte/line limits, truncates only the untrusted body, preserves complete markers, and fails closed when the trust envelope cannot fit.
- Authority-tag neutralization for remote-origin and subagent content, including custom categories and durable `runtime_context_data` wrappers; generic corpus content remains byte-exact except forged fence markers.
- Protected fence semantics and concise answer discipline in prompt `m8.5.1`.

966.body:
## What this changes

The loopback gateway's non-text rejection now carries `code: "unsupported_image_input"` next to its message. That is the only behaviour change.

`openjiuwen`'s image-modality probe (`openjiuwen/harness/image_modality_probe.py`, pinned rev `ad0c9df`) decides `image_input` by matching the exception it caught against two lists: an allowlist of error codes (`invalid_image_input`, `unsupported_image_input`, `unsupported_content_type`, `unsupported_image`, `unsupported_message_content_type`, .) and a list of message fragments (`images are not supported`, `image input not supported`, .). Our 400 carried `{ message, type }` only, so the verdict rested entirely on our wording staying inside the fragment list. It is inside it today; the code makes the classification independent of that.

The rejection keeps its position: after the unsupported-parameter, `messages`/`tools` shape, `tool_choice`/`n` and `stream_options` checks, and still above the capability-control ones. That last part is what makes the probe work at all - `_THINKING_DISABLED_EXTRA_BODY` sends `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`, `enable_thinking: false` and **`reasoning: {"enabled": false}`**, and that object is refused by the capability-control check, which sits below the image check. The test pins the probe's real body (image part + text + the object `reasoning`) rather than a reduced one.

A message entry that is not an object is now reported by the shape check (`Invalid gateway messages or tools`) instead of reaching the image check as a `TypeError`.

## What this does not claim

It does **not** close #956, and the description no longer says it does.

- The pre-change body already classified as a rejection: the OpenAI-compatible client raises `BadRequestError` whose text carries the response body, `_format_exception_detail` keeps it, `build_error` chains it, and `is_image_modality_rejection` reads `str(exc)` and then walks `__cause__`/`__context__`. "images are not supported" is one of the fragments, so the base message was already enough. This PR buys resilience to rewording, not a verdict flip.
- The reported `image_input=unknown (not cached)` line therefore does not come from this 400. The most likely source is the model entry that has no run behind it: `sd-default` points at the adapter's `/llm/default/v1`, which answers `503 {"error":{"message":"no run in progress: no model to use"}}` (`services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py:425`) - neither a code nor a fragment in either list, so `_run_probe` retries without the switches, gets the same 503, and returns `None`, which the warmup prints as `unknown (not cached)` (`jiuwenswarm/server/runtime/image_modality_warmup.py:161-164`). The full warmup line names the `(api_base, model)` it printed, which would settle it.
- The "repeated 400 on every start" half is also outside this file: the verdict cache is keyed on `(api_base, model_name)` (`probe_cache_key`), the run gateway listens on a fresh random port per run (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`, `server.listen(0, .)`), and a model-config change resets the cache before each run, so the probe re-runs per run by construction.

Both remaining halves need a decision this PR cannot make on its own: whether the probe should skip entries with no run behind them, and whether the per-run rejection should stop being re-probed. Tracked in #956.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts` | 57/58 pass; the one failure is the pre-existing `0o600` vs `0o666` file-mode assertion, unrelated to this change and failing on `main` here too |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api build` | clean |
| `markdownlint-cli2` | n/a - no doc changes in this PR |

The new test `a malformed request keeps its own diagnosis instead of the image verdict` pins the ordering: an image part plus `frequency_penalty` still answers `Unsupported gateway parameters: frequency_penalty`, an image part plus `n: 2` still answers `. one completion only`, and neither carries a `code`; `{ messages: [null] }` answers `Invalid gateway messages or tools`. Moving the image check back above the parameter check fails the suite.

Tests are tagged `os:linux`; ran locally with the platform filter in `test/support/tagged/compat.mjs` temporarily disabled and reverted, uncommitted. CI runs them natively.

Refs #956, #900.

967.body:
## Summary

Closes #958 by making the choice it asked for, and fixing the caller that was actually broken.

**The rule, now written down in `docs/{en,zh}/developer-docs/agent-backend.md`:** a 400 that names a thinking control the request carried gets exactly the named controls stripped and one retry. Which layer applies it — and whether it applies it yet — differs by sender. The non-stream boundary (`completeChatRequest`) stays a thin transport permanently, and every caller owns its own recovery.

Rebased onto current `main`: six files, no #956 commit (that one lives in #966).

## Why the transport stays dumb

A retry inside `completeChatRequest` consumes the 400 the caller needs. `services/api/src/session-naming.ts` retries that same 400 **and** raises `max_tokens` 64 → 16 384, because that retry is also the path for a gateway that ignores the control and truncates the title. Moving the recovery into the transport would answer the 400 before the caller could bump the budget — which is exactly why the attempt inside #901 turned those two session-naming tests red and was reverted instead of papered over.

## The actual defect, and the fix

The Settings connectivity probe (`services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`) owned **no** recovery. It sends the variant's control (`thinking: { type: "disabled" }` for `deepseek`), so on a gateway that refuses it the probe reported a broken model while the streaming half of the same compatibility check passed. That is #958's second acceptance criterion.

- **The retry strips what the 400 named from the request already built.** It does not switch the endpoint to `thinkingMode: "auto"`: `thinkingMode()` resolves through `constrainCatalogThinking()`, which rewrites a mode the catalog does not list to the model's declared default, so `auto` can rebuild the rejected body byte for byte (`kimi-k3` declares `modes: ["enabled"]`; both attempts would carry `reasoning_effort`). The probe deletes the named keys from `init.body` in its fetch wrapper on the retry — the same mechanism as the streamed sender's `withoutThinkingControls`.
- **The retry is gated on what actually went out.** A 400 names what the endpoint refused, never what this request sent, so `carriedThinkingControls(body)` (new, exported) gives the controls a serialized request carries, and the probe intersects it with the classifier's answer. A request that carried nothing keeps the provider's error instead of paying for a second request and reporting a strip that never happened.
- **The classifier is shared, not duplicated.** `rejectedThinkingControlFields(detail)` applies the streamed sender's rule (the provider's own `param` pointer, or a rejection phrase next to the field name; a complaint about a control's value or the state it was sent in proves nothing, and a body echo proves nothing). The private wrapper in `client.ts` now delegates to both exported functions, so the two senders cannot drift.
- **The doc says which streamed sender recovers.** Only `streamOpenAiTurn` does; `streamAnthropicTurn` retries nothing, and `openai-responses` sends `reasoning`, which is not one of the four control names. Both are named as the remaining gap.
- Callers that keep the provider's error on purpose (`papers.ts`, `evolution/llm-proxy.ts`) are named in the doc as a decision, not an oversight.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/model-connectivity.test.ts` | 37/37 pass, including three new cases: (1) a `deepseek` endpoint 400s `thinking` → retry without it, `ok`; (2) `kimi-k3` with an installed catalog snapshot → first body carries `reasoning_effort: "max"`, retry carries neither the field nor an identical body, `ok`; (3) a 400 naming a control the request never carried → exactly one request, `provider_error`/400 |
| `packages/model/src/client.test.ts` | 46/46 pass, including `remembers rejected thinking controls for an OpenAI-compatible gateway` — the classifier refactor keeps the streamed behaviour identical |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/model build`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api build` | clean |
| `markdownlint-cli2` on the two docs | 0 issues |

Tests are tagged `os:linux`; ran locally with the platform filter in `test/support/tagged/compat.mjs` temporarily disabled and reverted, uncommitted. CI runs them natively.

968.body:
## What this fixes

A native run whose **terminal** turn was cut at the output limit and called no tool used to end as `completed` with zero files and zero artifacts ??the shape #953 reports (0 workspace files, 0 artifacts, `finish_reason: "length"`, run status `completed`).

- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts` ends the loop and emits `completed { truncated: true }` for that turn.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts` only re-emitted it as `turn_truncated`.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` used the flag to pick fallback prose and then returned `"completed"`.

The JiuwenSwarm backend already refuses the same shape (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`, "Swarm ended with an unrecovered output limit"), so the two backends disagreed about what `completed` means. The native agent now records the truncated terminal turn from the same event stream and throws once the loop returns:

```
Native agent ended with an unrecovered output limit: the model was cut off by
max_tokens (16384) before it finished answering. Raise
SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_TOKENS and retry, or ask for a smaller step.
```

The run therefore reaches the existing `run.failed` path with `errorCode: semantic-error` ??same classification the Swarm backend's error already gets, so no new status value and no new failure code.

## Scope and non-goals

- **The keyword is `Refs #953` on purpose.** #953's Expected section asks for deliverable-producing behaviour: chunking the work, a shorter retry, or a continuation from the cut point. This PR implements none of them: it stops the false success from being reported as success, which is the step that has to exist before any recovery can be added. #953 stays open for the no-deliverables half and for the maintainer's decision on terminal-status semantics (F3).

- **This is the false success, not the token budget.** A truncated turn that *did* call tools keeps its existing recovery path (the loop continues); only the shape that ends the run is refused.
- **No prompt steering.** Option 1 in the issue (chunk the work across turns) is `skills/evolve-design` behaviour, not a runtime status fix.
- **No output recovery on the native loop.** The Swarm patch `0007` retries twice before failing; porting that is a separate change and needs its own budget/duplication rules. Fail-closed first, recovery second.
- `turn_truncated` is still emitted before the throw, so telemetry and the stream reducer are unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/native-agent/native-agent.test.ts` | 44/44 pass, including the new case: a streamer returning a truncated turn with no tool call makes `execute()` reject with `/unrecovered output limit/`, naming `max_tokens` and `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_TOKENS` |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api build` | clean |
| `markdownlint-cli2` on the two docs | 0 issues |

Tests are tagged `os:linux`; ran locally with the platform filter in `test/support/tagged/compat.mjs` temporarily disabled and reverted, uncommitted. CI runs them natively.

## On the "needs information" findings

The triage asked which executor produced the reported run, and whether the Swarm path can even show this shape. It cannot ??that path fails closed ??so the report is either the native executor or a stale install of the Swarm patched code (`jiuwen_swarm/README.md`: patches apply at setup, and `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh` returns early when the instance is already up). Either way the native path is the one that still reports a cut-off run as done, and that is what this PR changes. The stale-install hypothesis is unaffected: an old process keeps its old behaviour until it is restarted.

Refs #953.

969.author: qingkwl
969.body:
Closes the §2 checkbox of #897 (first-run bytecode completeness). #834's code is reviewed; this carries the part deliberately left out of it.

## What #897 §2 asks for

> Write a manifest or count of the precompiled set **at assemble time** and check it **at bootstrap**, so an incomplete set (quarantined file, partial copy, interrupted unpack) **fails the build or names itself at first launch** instead of surfacing as an `ImportError` at first tool use.

Both halves are here, because either one alone leaves the other failure mode open:

- A build fix alone does not help an installer **already in the field**, nor one damaged **after** the build (partial copy, interrupted unpack, an AV quarantine).
- A bootstrap fix alone still lets a bad payload be **built and shipped** in the first place.

## The defect this replaces

`treeHasPycache` (`bootstrap.ts`) answers "is there **ANY** `.pyc` under here" and short-circuits on the first hit. release6 shipped **1,384 `.pyc` where the build had compiled ~37,000** — the build environment exported `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX`, and `compileall` (which spread `process.env`) redirected every bytecode file into a mirror tree *outside* the payload while still **exiting 0**. So the envs tree still looked complete to that helper, bootstrap **skipped** the remedial compile, and the missing modules only failed later as an `ImportError` the first time a tool imported one — the exact failure mode §2 says must not happen.

At the default install root the remedial compile is not even runnable (`63 + 1 + 192 + 14 > 259`), so a complete shipped `.pyc` set is load-bearing.

## What the change does

This is a single squashed commit (`c3b29003`) — the `main` ruleset allows only `squash` and `rebase` merges, and the mirrored merge request carries `stat/needs-squash`. The content is byte-identical to the four-commit history it replaces (same tree, `b9175fc9`); the sections below are organised by what the code now does rather than by commit, but each constraint in the third section traces to a specific review finding, which is why it looks the way it does.

### Fail the build

- **`payloadCompileEnv()`** strips `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` (and warns) before any python the build spawns. `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` is deliberately **not** stripped: measured inert here (`compileall` still writes its `.pyc` with the variable set — it only suppresses the *implicit* write that importing performs). The test pins that exclusion so re-adding the name goes red with a pointer to re-measure.
- **A6 bytecode-budget gate** piggybacks on A5's existing tree walk (no second pass over ~95,000 files), asserts the payload's `.pyc`/`.py` ratio clears **90%**, and `fail()`s the build otherwise. It prints on **every** build — coverage is a trend quantity, and a budget nobody sees eroding fails all at once. A ratio, not an absolute floor, so it survives upstream churn instead of rotting in the unsafe direction. Both halves of the claim are measured rather than asserted from the source text: it runs in a real build (`RESULT=A6_EXECUTED_IN_REAL_BUILD`), and it fails closed on the incident shape and on an empty walk — see the last three entries under *Measured evidence*.

### Name it at first launch

- **assemble** writes a `bytecode` block into `resources/version.json` — py/pyc counts from the **same** walk A6 gates on (no second traversal) plus per-region buckets. This is the count §2 asks the build to record.
- **bootstrap** gains `countBytecode()` (full iterative walk, no short-circuit) and `readPayloadBytecodeManifest()` (`null` when `version.json` is absent or predates the field, so the check degrades to the ratio rather than passing blind). It replaces `treeHasPycache()`, which answered "is there **ANY** `.pyc` under here" and short-circuited on the first hit, and on a shortfall logs **which tree, how incomplete, and why it matters** before any `ImportError` can.

### Three constraints each finding added

The first two review rounds (zhaozhaozz P1/P2/P3, HongyeZhou required-change, agent-ci-infra-bot F1/F2/F3/F4, F3/F4 confirmed by yuanzhou75 against the code) each found a way this check could look green and judge nothing. All three are now closed:

- **Reachability (P1/F1, then F3).** Wiring the verdict only into the copy branch left it unreachable on every real install: `main.ts:651`/`:887` set `SCIENCE_AGENT_IN_PLACE_ENVS=1` before `bootstrapPackaged`, so every packaged start takes the in-place branch. My original scoping note claimed the in-place tree was out of scope because it is read-only and not copied — **that was wrong**: in-place mode runs from `paths.envsTemplate`, exactly the region the manifest records. Fixed by extracting `judgeBytecodeCoverage()` and calling it from **both** branches. F3 then found the *gate* had the same shape of defect: gating on `needsUnpack()`, which compares only `stamp.installRoot`, means an upgrade — which **keeps** that identity, since `installer.nsh:130-141` restores `$INSTDIR` from the registry and `wizard-data-dir.ts:22` pins the data dir — skips the judgement on the one launch that *replaces* the payload. The gate is now a **separate** predicate `needsBytecodeJudgement()` comparing `payloadIdentity()` (`repoCommit` + `builtAt` from the `version.json` the build already writes) against the stamp; `needsUnpack` is untouched, so the unpack decision is not changed silently, and a stamp predating the field is judged rather than trusted. The walk is paid once per **payload**.
- **The ratio is blind in both directions (P2, then F4).** Dropping a whole directory removes `.py` and `.pyc` together, so the ratio stayed at 99.9% while the tree lost 16% of its files. `UNPACKED_MIN_COUNT_SHARE = 0.95` compares the walk against the build's recorded count, applied **after** the ratio so a stale-high manifest can only make the verdict stricter, never rescue a bad one. F4 then found the *other* direction: coverage is `pyc/py`, so deleting **sources** makes it look *healthier* — half the `.py` gone read as ~200% and passed both limits, while a PEP 3147 `.pyc` is unusable without its source. The same tolerance therefore applies to the `.py` count too. Measured boundary on the real region: 306 sources silent at 95.00%, 307 caught at 94.99%.
- **The remedial compile must not inherit the redirect it exists to undo (P3/F2).** `compileEnv` was a raw `{...process.env}` spread; on a machine exporting `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` the recovery would write bytecode outside the tree, still exit 0, and the stamp would freeze the gap in. Now built with `payloadCompileEnv(process.env, { warn: log })`.

Evidence moved from source-text assertions to **behavioural** tests that drive `bootstrapPackaged` for real, because source-text guards are precisely what stayed green through P1 and F3.

The verdict also returns **which** limit fired, so the log promises only what the remedial compile can do: missing caches are recompilable, missing sources are not, and claiming otherwise is a log that reports a fix which never happened.

## Scope and cost

The judgement walks the **`envs-template` region** — measured **6,119 `.pyc` for 6,124 `.py` = 99.9%** on release6, ~**750ms** — and runs on the first launch of each payload. The read-only targets *outside* that region (the stdlib, the jw venv at ~3.2s) keep the cheap per-target probe, on purpose: the region verdict does not cover them, so a W4-style skip of one target must still self-heal. A relaunch of the same payload short-circuits and pays nothing, which is what the "first run must not get slower" constraint allows.

The one way a healthy copy legitimately differs from the build count is NSIS silently dropping `.pyc` whose path breaches `MAX_PATH` (#W15, measured worst case **one** file). At 0.95 a normal install may lose **305 of 6,119** files before this warns, so the known-good case keeps ~300x headroom and the warning cannot cry wolf.

## Tests

- `test/pyc-budget.test.ts` (**35**): the verdict against **both measured release6 trees** (broken `1,384/37,998 = 3.6%` fails, rebuild `37,324/37,998 = 98.2%` passes), the W15 tolerance, manifest-absent and manifest-bogus paths, the `.py`-side limit and its shared boundary, plus wiring guards that assert each source anchor actually matched (a guard that silently anchors on nothing is worse than none).
- `test/bootstrap.test.ts` (**29**): drive `bootstrapPackaged` **for real** in both modes — near-empty payload, whole-directory loss, sources-lost-with-caches-kept, healthy payload, valid-stamp short-circuit, **upgrade at the same install root re-judges**, a payload-less stamp is judged not trusted, missing manifest.

## Measured evidence (`logs/w25-evidence/`)

> Path note: this directory is **not part of the PR tree** — it sits outside the repo, and the repo's own `logs/` is gitignored, so the entries below cannot be opened from the PR. They are listed so the measurements are auditable and re-runnable, and because the conclusions above are stated as measurements rather than as claims. What *is* in the tree and re-runnable by any reviewer: `win_desktop/test/pyc-budget.test.ts`, `win_desktop/test/bootstrap.test.ts`, `win_desktop/scripts/lib/pyc-budget.mjs` and `win_desktop/scripts/assemble-backend.mjs`. Committing the probes was deliberately not done here, since it would change the tree and dismiss the two existing approvals on a byte-identical squash.

- `probe-bootstrap-disagree.mjs`: a synthesised partial tree makes the **old** gate say "complete" while the **new** gate says "0.3%" — they disagree, so the fix is not decoration.
- `probe-a6-e2e.mjs`: the **cause** reproduced for real — `compileall` run under an exported `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` writes its `.pyc` outside the tree while still exiting 0, which is release6 at miniature scale. Three arms: control passes, the redirect is caught, `payloadCompileEnv()` prevents it. **Scope limit, stated because the filename oversells it:** its walk is a replica (its own line 42 reads "Replica of assemble-backend.mjs's A6 walk") and it calls `pycBudgetVerdict` directly, so it exercises the *library*, **not** the gate block inside `assemble-backend.mjs`. The next two entries close that gap.
- `a6-reachability-assemble.log`: a **real** `assemble-backend.mjs` run at this head (`HEAD=c3b29003`, logged; `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` explicitly unset; 40m22s). The gate printed `A6 bytecode budget: 37324 .pyc for 37998 .py = 98.2% (limit 90.0%)` and the build ran on to `done — payload pieces`; verdict line `RESULT=A6_EXECUTED_IN_REAL_BUILD`. The `version.json` it wrote carries the same counts (`{"py":37998,"pyc":37324}`). This is the reachability arm — a gate nobody calls is dead code, and no assertion on the source text can tell, so it was measured by running the build.
- `prove-a6-negative-control.mjs`: the teeth arm. It **executes the gate's own source text** — located by anchor and sliced out of `assemble-backend.mjs`, not transcribed, because a hand-copied block drifts from the gate it claims to test — with a `fail()` that exits. Measured: this build's payload `(37998, 37324)` → no exit; the release6 shape `(37998, 1384)` → **exit 1**, `only 3.6% … (limit 90.0%)`; an empty walk `(0, 0)` → **exit 1**, `the tree walk counted 0 .py files, so this measurement measured nothing`. A mutation sentinel strips the block's only failure guard (`if (!verdict.ok)` → `if (false)`) and requires all three verdicts to flip, because a check that passes no matter what is worse than no check; that sentinel caught two real defects in this harness before it was trustworthy.
- `verify-real-tree.mjs`: `countBytecode` on the **real** release6 region matches an independent walk and is judged healthy (no false positive).
- `probe-f4-source-share.mjs`: the F4 blind spot reproduced at the head the bot filed it against (`1eeef872`, now squashed into this commit), and the calibrated boundary after the fix.
- `mutate-inplace-wiring.mjs` (3/3) and `mutate-f3f4.mjs` (**4/4**) have teeth. The latter's M1 is a **faithful** mutant: it leaves the guarded line byte-identical and breaks only reachability, so the behavioural test goes red while every source-text guard stays green — the precise shape that slipped through round 1.

## Regression

`win_desktop` UT **214 pass**, architecture **340 files OK**, repo-root scripts **43 pass**, `tsc --noEmit` clean. The four failures zhaozhaozz reported (two Windows path-separator assertions, the repo-root test, `killStackTree`) do not reproduce here and are not introduced by this change.

No behaviour change on a healthy payload: the first launch still skips the remedial compile — it now *proves* coverage first, for the payload actually installed, instead of assuming it.

## CI

Repository-side checks are green on this head (`c3b29003`), including the one check this repo actually requires: the `main` ruleset lists exactly one required status check, **`merge-gate`**, and it passes (job `128291933652`).

Settled tally on this head, from a single workflow run `42334507702` (`conclusion: success`): **13 pass / 1 fail / 4 skipping**. The four skips are `Binary release`, `Docker image`, `L3 real E2E` and `L4/L5 real E2E` — and skipping is the *passing* condition for them, not an anomaly: `gate()` in `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` pushes a problem unless those jobs report `skipped` under the `pr` profile. The one fail is the external `CodeCheck (GitCode)` described below.

`CodeCheck (GitCode)` reports `failure` and does not block. I previously wrote that it "failed identically on the previous head", which was a bad argument — comparing only my own heads proves nothing about the gate. The control group does:

- **PR #929** (GitCode `!583`, a 3-line `services/api` change by another author) got `CodeCheck（静态检查）FAILED` on **two** separate pipeline runs, and was **merged** anyway on 2026-11-06 (`face1d40`).
- Across the last **40** mirrored merge requests, **38** are `ci-successful` and only **2** are `ci-failed` — this one and #929. So the gate is not globally broken, and failing it is survivable.
- The failing sub-item is isolated: the pipeline's own table reports `SCA（开源合规）PASSED`, `Anti-poison（防投毒）PASSED`, `Blacklist（禁用词）PASSED`, and only the static-check sub-item `FAILED`. Its API returns `state: "no pass"` with `failData: null` and `taskCount: 0` — no findings are published, and the detail dashboard (`openlibing.com`) sits behind a WAF.
- I also tested the obvious local hypothesis and it does not hold: non-ASCII characters in added lines. The baseline `bootstrap.ts` this PR builds on already carries 30 such lines (25 em-dashes, 6 arrows) and passes the gate, and #929's 3 added lines contain none.

I am not claiming to know why the static check fails — that needs someone with access to the openlibing dashboard. What I can show is that it is not a gate this repo enforces, that it has failed on changes smaller and less invasive than this one without stopping them, and that the local hypotheses I could test are ruled out.

One CI artefact worth naming, because it looked like a second red on an earlier head of this PR and is not a code failure. The pre-squash head `76408f5f` had **two** `CI` workflow runs. The cancelled duplicate (`42328619686`) shows `merge-gate` as `failure`, but its own annotation says why — `Unable to download artifact(s): Artifact not found for name: mocked-e2e-plan`, because every upstream job in that run was cancelled. `gate()` in `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` then correctly reports `CI gate failed: policy: cancelled; l1: cancelled; …`; a cancelled run *should* fail the gate rather than pass vacuously. The surviving run on that head (`42328619676`) has `merge-gate` **green**. The current head `c3b29003` has exactly **one** run, so this artefact does not recur here.

971.body:
The BiomniBench-DA L5 execution set contains 45 active cases, with both the generator and rubric judge set to `enabled` thinking and `low` effort. This change also addresses the `da-11-1` delivery failure: a stream ending inside tool-call JSON can now use Swarm's existing bounded correction path, and the case requests incremental document writes to reduce oversized tool calls. The issue's broader coverage, flake governance, A/B validation and release-duration targets remain open.

Refs #817

## da-11-1 delivery recovery

Run [42340397412](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42340397412/job/128306684470) recorded an oversized `run_shell` response hitting the 16,384-output-token limit, then another unparseable call. The second response was HTTP 200 with no usage; code tracing identifies the missing-completion guard as a path that bypasses existing argument recovery. Raw upstream SSE was not retained, so the exact missing event is not independently proven from the log.

- For a clean EOF with unparseable tool arguments, withhold **all** calls from that turn and ask the model to re-issue them through the existing maximum of two corrections. Valid calls/plain answers without completion, corrupt SSE, housekeeping and requesters lacking the recovery boundary remain rejected. No partial JSON execution or whole-case replay is introduced.
- Add `da-11-1`-only delivery guidance: write `trace.md` and `answer.txt` in small sections, inspect existing content after an interrupted write and append only missing content. Preserve the original scientific instruction and full required outputs.
- Include the failed run's original error in benchmark failures; retain shutdown evidence without replacing that error with `Session cleanup unverified`. Stop launching shutdown snapshots once the shared deadline has expired.
- Add streaming/unary regressions for withheld calls, successful correction, missing usage and fail-closed boundaries, plus browser journey `LR-18` for clean-EOF recovery with exactly one real shell execution. Extend prompt-scope and shutdown-deadline regressions.

This update does not change HTTP-provider retries or the other three reported case failures. Missing provider usage remains missing; billing completeness and scientific scoring gates remain enforced. A new real run is required to establish that `da-11-1` completes reliably.

## L5 selection and reasoning configuration

- Exclude `da-1-3`, `da-1-4`, `da-17-1`, `da-17-5` and `da-17-3` through one checked-in exclusion list. Preserve the pinned 50-case upstream manifest for provenance.
- Apply the active case set consistently to collection, matrix generation, complete-suite accounting and the resumable serial driver. The full real L5 plan changes from 69 to 64 cases; all 45 selected Biomni cases still require valid results.
- Pin generator and judge thinking to `enabled` with reasoning effort `low` for Biomni workers in the reusable real-E2E workflow, manual validation workflow and serial driver. Update selection/gate regression checks and documentation.

## Review corrections

- Set both thinking modes explicitly to `enabled`, alongside effort `low`, in the serial driver and Biomni workflow workers. This also covers serial evaluation-only recovery and prevents inherited `disabled` mode from making the judge configuration invalid.
- Preserve the two historical **50-case** A3 observations. Explicitly normalize only additive resource budgets by `45/50` before applying the existing threshold ratios. Effective references: tokens 175,589,740.8; tool rounds 1,837.8; total research time 70,888,687.5143097 ms. Mean score 67.7 and P95 remain unscaled, population-shifted historical references, not measured 45-case results; recalibration remains outstanding.
- Report `scope: public-45-active`, retain `dataset_scope: public-50` and the excluded IDs, and publish historical/effective references and scaling in the gate artifacts.
- Document that the exclusions and fixed low setting are the submitter's explicit scope/budget policy. No per-case invalidity/flake evidence or A/B conclusion is claimed. Maintainer acceptance of this policy remains a review decision. Both workflows ignore thinking mode/effort repository variables for Biomni workers; a Biomni A/B needs a separate configuration change.

## Validation

Current head: `1db615cdd23880040377e2848a2c5d7695003a38` (one commit).

For the delivery recovery update, syntax-only checks passed for all nine changed TypeScript files; `git diff --check` passed; E2E metadata validation inspected 88 spec files with 0 errors and 11 existing legacy warnings. The regression tests and `LR-18` journey were added but **not executed**. No local UT/ST/E2E or paid L5/A/B runs were executed, as requested. CI at this new head is still required.

The preceding configuration review update at superseded SHA `2845c009480afd22382c1c8890fe7f927cd6cc31` used JavaScript syntax parsing, Python AST parsing, JSON parsing, threshold arithmetic inspection and `git diff --check`; it did not run tests.

Historical tested commit: `0b58bd88ee1ab445f2be1a01f1b578518f83c9e0` (superseded; the results below do not validate the current head).

Local Linux validation used the four documented slice commands on the commit above. These are the completed results; no passing full-suite result is claimed.

| Slice | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 | PASS |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 6530 | 6501 | 6498 | 3 | FAIL; 29 additional cases not run because local Swarm startup failed |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 51 | 51 | 49 | 2 | FAIL |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | — | — | — | — | Incomplete; local execution stopped during startup |

The UT failures were a local fault-injection timeout, a logical/physical checkout path mismatch after relocating the temporary checkout, and a Runner execution-state timeout. ST failures and these timeout failures have not been established as regressions or as pre-existing failures. The three changed Biomni test files completed in the UT run. PR CI is still required.

An additional `pnpm test:shared` attempt stopped during collection with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/markdown-math.test.ts:16`; no test summary was produced. The same source-auditor error was reproduced directly on unmodified `main` at `b31f74eb368a0e07848c2aa72acf9451348471bb`, using byte-identical math-test and auditor files. This is a focused baseline reproduction, not a completed main test suite.

## E2E user journeys

**NOT RUN — current head:** the new mocked browser journey `LR-18` submits a research request through the UI, receives a clean EOF inside tool arguments, then requires a completed answer, exactly one execution of the corrected call and no execution of partial arguments. Existing disconnect and bounded-exhaustion journeys remain in the same suite. These journeys require an exclusive Swarm task stack; they were not run per the request to avoid local tests. Executed: 0; no PASS result is claimed for the new behavior.

**FAIL — historical full L5 run at superseded SHA `0b58bd88ee1ab445f2be1a01f1b578518f83c9e0`:** [run 42236770100](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42236770100), manual validation, profile `l5`, backend `jiuwenswarm`, maximum parallelism 4. This drives the browser/local-stack scientific task through final artifacts and rubric scoring.

- Expected: 45 active Biomni cases, with the five excluded IDs absent and both model efforts set to `low`. Actual: the frozen plan and runtime configuration match those expectations.
- Complete real plan: planned 64, executed 63, passed 19, failed 44, skipped 0; one result missing.
- Biomni outcomes: 40 completed research and delivery but the judge returned HTTP 403; four research runs ended with a model-stream `network` error; the `da-15-2` hosted runner lost communication and uploaded no result. Valid scored Biomni cases: 0/45.

Judge authorization/access and model-stream failures remain unresolved. These results do not establish scientific-score non-regression, a thinking-mode A/B conclusion, or the issue's five-hour release target.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: Swarm can recover a clean EOF inside tool arguments without executing partial calls; Biomni L5 uses the requested active-case and reasoning policy.

Compatibility and migration: no product API or configuration migration.

972.body: The design search used to open as an overlay that covered the transcript, and its runs lived in a shelf at the foot of the conversation. Reading the search meant hiding the turns that produced it, a finished run had no home while the panel was closed, and the header carried a runtime capsule that named the runtime rather than the run. The right column now has a 任务 tab that owns the search end to end. ## The run in the panel The tab lists the Session's searches and shows the selected one — the run the reader picked, else the one that wants attention, else the newest — with its header, score chart, tree and candidate drawer. The tab exists only while the Session has runs, and it disappears with the last one. A command sent from this window opens the run it created once the list re-reads, because the list is idle until something is active; a reload or a session switch does not move the panel, since the search is not news to the reader who came back to it. The run's card at the foot of the transcript and 会话设置's row both open that same view. The shelf, the overlay, the candidate table and the header capsule are removed. ## The tree The tree is a drawing that can be read at its own scale: dragging pans, the wheel zooms, and the zoom is anchored at the pointer rather than at the corner. Panning is bounded so part of the drawing always stays in sight, and a zoom the reader set survives a panel resize. The rest of the layout is unchanged; the zoom buttons and the engine log strip are gone. A node opens its detail on click. The viewport used to capture the pointer on every press, and a captured pointer makes the browser dispatch the click to the capturing element, so the click reached the viewport and not the node under it; capture now starts with the first move that is actually a pan. ## The composer The setup dialog no longer sends the command it collected. It places `/evolve-design` and its flags in the composer as a token and leaves the sentence to the reader, because the goal is prose and sending is a question about the sentence only. The token is out of flow so the wrapped lines start at the field's margin instead of indenting under it, and it scrolls with the first line past the field's max height. The token can be taken back: its ✕ drops the flags and keeps the sentence, because a reader who changed their mind meant to stop the search, not to lose what they were going to say. The shell drops the seed when the session changes as well — the composer outlives that switch, and a token left behind would turn the next ordinary message into a long, costly search nobody asked for. Both places that place the caret after filling the field — the welcome page's starter prompt and a design's command — now share one `focusAtEnd` helper instead of carrying identical copies. ## The chart The best node wears the handoff's crown instead of a trophy — as the chart's marker and legend key, on the tree badge, in the node list and in the drawer header — and its label is 最佳 / Best. The drawer's score tile keeps the trophy. Pointing at a plotted node draws a dashed rule down the plot and a card with the node, its layer and its score; the best node adds the crown and the tag, and a failed node answers with its verdict instead of a score. The hit areas are larger than the dots, the card flips at the chart's edges, and focusing a node with the keyboard opens the same card. Pressing a plotted node opens its detail — the same drawer a row of the node list opens — and the point carries no focus rectangle: a focused point answers the way a hovered one does, with the card and the enlarged dot. The key that used to say 显著节点 / Significant now says 得分节点 / Scored: non-significant nodes are no longer drawn, so the old name asked the reader to notice a distinction the chart no longer makes. ## The budget Three rows, because three gates can end a search: the tokens spent, the time on the clock, and the expansions dispatched against the plan. The cost row is gone — nothing in the system prices a token, every run carries `maxCostCents: 0`, and a bar that can only ever say "no price table configured" is not a budget. The clock row is 耗时 rather than 延时. ## The run card in the transcript A session's runs are fetched a beat after the messages they sit under. The card now follows the transcript's own growth while the reader is at the bottom, so opening a session with a run no longer leaves the card half hidden under the composer. ## Wording 代际 is replaced by 层数 throughout the panel: 代际 is borrowed from genetics and reads as jargon beside a node's own index. The overview counts 层数, and a node's tag reads 层数 01. ## The narrow column The panel's narrow-column rules were `@container` queries with no container declared, so they never matched. At the panel's floor — 568px on a 1440px window — the five overview cells collided and their numbers spilled over the borders. The detail column is now the container those rules were written to ask about, so the overview reflows instead of reading the window's width, which says nothing about the column's. Two columns was not the only step it needed. At the default 720px panel the five cells are 128px wide and the token count needs about 158, so the last cell's value was clipped by the card's `overflow: hidden` — the one reading that only appears once a search has spent a six-figure number of tokens. Below 880px the row is three cells across; below 620 it is the two the floor needs. The search tree's nodes also draw their selection ring on `:focus-visible`; they are tab stops and said nothing about the keyboard's position. ## The checkpoint card The band names the card's state, the counter sits at the right and counts only the checkpoints that ask — the closing record is written after the run and answers nothing. A record folds like an answered card. It asks nothing, its body is the longest text the transcript holds, and the run that walked four steps should read as four lines rather than four screens: the header keeps the step and the headline, and the body is one click away. The folded shape is one set of rules keyed on `is-folded`; `is-answered` and `is-record` name the state and are left for a state-specific tint. ## Screenshots Captured in the desktop app running against this machine's live control plane (the Vite front end on `:5174`, the API on `:4312`), in 中文 and English. The run is a real PUCT search — 16 expansions planned, 15 dispatched, 586,941 tokens, 28m59s — from the session **PUCT 无损文本压缩实现**. **Before** is the same live stack with the front end at the merge base `b31f74e`; **after** is the front end of this branch, `947ad817`. ### 中文 **搜索从会话里搬进右栏的任务页。** 之前会话顶端是一条 shelf 和标题栏的运行时胶囊，打开搜索是一个盖住对话的浮层；现在是一张卡片留在会话底部，打开它只是右栏换一个模式，对话仍然可读。 | 前（`b31f74e`）：shelf 与标题栏胶囊 | 后（本 PR）：会话底部的卡片 | | --- | --- | | | | | 前（`b31f74e`）：盖住对话的浮层 | 后（本 PR）：右栏的任务页 | | --- | --- | | | | **任务页。** 概览读的是本次搜索的成绩、层数与 Token；得分图把每个候选画在它的扩展次数上，指针停在点上给出节点、层数与分数——这里是带皇冠的 `最佳` 节点；下面是树、节点列表与预算。 | 概览、得分图与节点列表 | 图上悬停：最佳节点 | | --- | --- | | | | | 搜索树与节点列表 | 树 + 预算 | | --- | --- | | | | **预算三行。** Token、耗时、节点：三条能把搜索停下来的闸门。费用那一行不在了——系统里没有任何东西给 token 定价。时钟一行叫 `耗时`，深度叫 `层数`。 | 节点详情 | 代码变更全屏 | | --- | --- | | | | **输入框里的设计命令。** 对话框不再直接发送：`/evolve-design` 连同 flags 成为输入框里的一个 token，句子留给读者继续写。token 带 ✕，改主意的人能去掉它而保住自己写的句子。 | 入口：会话设置里的 程序演进实验 | 新建程序演进实验 | | --- | --- | | | | | 种下命令后的输入框（带 ✕） | | --- | | | ### English **The search leaves the transcript for a task tab.** The shelf strip and the header capsule are gone; the run keeps one card at the foot of the conversation, and opening it changes the right column instead of covering the conversation. | Before (`b31f74e`) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | | | | | Before (`b31f74e`): the overlay over the conversation | After: the task tab | | --- | --- | | | | **The task tab.** The overview reads this search's best score, its generations and its token count; the chart plots every candidate against the expansion that produced it, and pointing at one names the node, its layer and its score — here the best node, under the crown. Below it, the tree, the node list and the budget. | The overview with the chart | Pointing at the best node | | --- | --- | | | | | The tree with the node list | The tree with the budget | | --- | --- | | | | **The budget's three rows.** Tokens, elapsed, nodes: the three gates that can end a search. There is no cost row — nothing in the system prices a token — the clock row says Elapsed, and a node's depth reads Gen. | A node's detail | The code changes, full screen | | --- | --- | | | | **The design command in the composer.** The dialog no longer sends: `/evolve-design` and its flags arrive as a token in the field and the sentence is left to the reader. The token carries a ✕, so somebody who changes their mind can drop the flags and keep what they were going to say. | The way in: a new session's settings menu | A new evolution run | | --- | --- | | | | | The composer after the dialog seeds the command (with its ✕) | | --- | | | ### What these do not show - The states that need a hand on the pointer rather than a capture: the tree after a drag-pan, a wheel zoom, and a resize that keeps the zoom; the hover card flipping at the chart's edges; the keyboard focus ring on a plotted point or a tree node. They are covered by the unit suite and `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`, not by a still frame. - The before side of the composer: at `b31f74e` the dialog sent the command itself, so a "before" capture would have started a real search on this stack. The after side is the last still above. - A Session with no searches: the tab is not drawn, which the same fixture asserts in `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`. ## Validation - Desktop unit suite: 842 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (`apps/desktop`: `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`), run on `2c822748`. - Typecheck: `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json` clean. - Repository layers, run on this host at `947ad81` (the last head before the checkpoint, marker and folding follow-ups): `pnpm ci:ut` planned 6,606 / executed 6,606 / passed 6,593 / failed 13; `pnpm ci:st` planned 51 / passed 49 / failed 2; `pnpm ci:e2e` reported BLOCKED — the isolated stack did not become healthy.
