973.body:
Closes #953.

#968 landed the fail-closed half — a native run whose terminal turn was cut at the output limit stopped reporting `completed`, and threw instead. This PR lands the other half of the issue's "Expected behavior": the native loop now retries that cut-off turn before it fails, so the run can still produce deliverables.

## What changes

- `packages/runtime-core` gains a provider-neutral `outputRecovery` port: when a turn is truncated with no tool call, the loop appends a feedback message (built by the composition root) and reassembles context, up to 2 extra attempts, before falling through to the existing fail-closed path.
- `services/api/src/native-agent` wires the port: the feedback asks the model to stop expanding and perform ONE small useful action, with a bounded excerpt of the unfinished text (marked as not a completed result). Aligned with JiuwenSwarm patch `0007` (`MAX_RECOVERIES = 2`, the truncated turn is not replayed as a completed answer, no tool from the truncated response executes).
- `packages/context` relaxes the `recovery` type from the single `model-input-overflow` rebuild to a general `{ attempt, reason }` so an output-limit rebuild reuses the same forced-compaction path; context-trace filenames reflect the attempt.

## Behavior

- A truncated turn that **did** call a tool keeps its existing path (the loop continues) — unchanged.
- A truncated terminal turn now gets 2 recovery attempts; if the model still returns a truncated, tool-call-free turn afterward, the run throws `Native agent ended with an unrecovered output limit` exactly as #968 does.

## Tests

`packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.test.ts`:
- a truncated tool-call-free turn is retried with output-limit feedback before completing
- output-limit recovery exhausts and still reports the truncated turn for fail-closed handling

Local pnpm test runs were not possible in this environment (no standalone Node/pnpm toolchain), so the CI merge-gate is the verification. The existing #968 fail-closed test still holds: its streamer keeps returning a truncated turn, so recovery exhausts before failing.

975.author: ink999107
975.body:
Reopening a Session that had approved an artifact download showed a permission card whose buttons could never work. The download had in fact run: the catalog recorded the answer and the artifact plan was approved. But the run's event log held only the `permission.required` snapshot, so replaying the run rebuilt a pending request inside a run that had already terminated. Every artifact-download approval left that residue behind, and so did an approval-mode switch that cleared pending requests.

## Publish the resolution onto the run that asked

`permission.required` was the only half of the artifact-download flow that reached the run stream. The decision endpoint and the approval-mode switch now publish the matching `permission.resolved` through the same `publishRunEvent` choke point every other event uses.

The owning run is not always `executionId`: for a subagent request it is the parent turn, and Reviewer MCP tools report a tool-call id. `publishResolvedPermissions` resolves a run id directly, maps a subagent to its parent turn, and otherwise falls back to the run still in flight. Requests this process saw raised are remembered when the `permission.required` is published, so the owner survives the execution id no longer matching by decision time.

The answer is written once. `waitForPermissionDecision` already emits the resolution from inside the run's wait, and a second path publishing the same decision would duplicate it on the stream, so `publishRunEvent` drops a duplicate `permission.resolved` and returns a live-only record to the caller that reads it. A request with no run to own it is skipped with a warning rather than failing the decision.

## Reconcile a replayed pending request with the catalog

The backend fix stops new residue but cannot rewrite logs already written. When a replay still ends on a pending request, the desktop reads `GET /api/permission-requests?sessionId=` once and lets the catalog's terminal answer replace the replayed snapshot. The merge only touches entries the replay already holds, so a Session-wide list cannot grow a card in a run that never asked; a request the catalog still calls pending keeps its card, and an answer the replay already carries is never undone. With no pending request in any replay, no request is made at all.

## Validation

Each layer ran locally on the commit being pushed, and every failing case was rerun on a pristine detached `main` worktree to separate a pre-existing failure from a regression here.

- **UT** (`pnpm ci:ut`): planned 6606, executed 6606, passed 6591, failed 15, skipped 0. All 15 are pre-existing: 5 in `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts`, 5 in `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts`, 1 in `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` (this host's bubblewrap 0.6 lacks `--disable-userns`), 1 in `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` (missing `context.captured`, reproduced on `main`), 1 in `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`, and 2 that pass on a rerun (`scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, a transient ETIMEDOUT, passes standalone on both this branch and `main`) and `check:research-python-ut` (uv cache lock timeout on this host).
- **ST** (`pnpm ci:st`): planned 51, executed 51, passed 50, failed 1. The failure is `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` (`fetch-runtime.mjs`) and reproduces identically on unmodified `main`.
- **New tests**: `apps/desktop/tests/permission-card-residue.test.ts` replays the run log that produced the reported card (`run 27e45b93…`, request `3c3fde16…`): a pending snapshot in a completed run folds to one pending request, reconciling it with the catalog's `allowed` answer removes it, a catalog-pending request keeps its card, and a run whose log already carries the resolution needs no catalog read. `apps/desktop/tests/permission-reconcile.test.ts` covers the merge rules, and the API tests assert the decision endpoint and the approval-mode switch publish exactly one `permission.resolved` onto the owning run.

## E2E user journeys

`pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked browser suite, JiuwenSwarm backend, local stack) on the commit being pushed: planned 133, executed 133, passed 127, failed 6, blocked 0, skipped 0. The four batches ran on their own isolated stacks: research 20/20, literature 6/6, governed 5/5 (including both governed-download approval journeys), standard 96/102.

All six failures reproduce on an unmodified `main` worktree built from source with its own `node_modules` and `dist`, so none is a regression here:

- `journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen` J309 fails on `main` with the same measurement (paragraph width 774 px against a 760 px bound).
- `journey-error-diagnostics` (en and zh-CN) passes alone on `main`, but fails identically on `main` when the `journey-empty-state-actions` group runs first: those journeys end by deleting the Project they created, so the next journey reaches the onboarding screen with no session and never finds `.session-bar-session`.
- `journey-jiuwen-configuration-on-demand` and `journey-model-connect-wizard` fail on `main` in the same steps.
- `journey-prepare-environment` J3 reports `managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)` on this host, where micromamba cannot be fetched; the failure is identical on `main`.

The permission paths themselves are green: the governed-download approval journeys, the permission-decision journey and the reviewer approval journeys all pass. Verification that the fix answers the reported case is in the UT layer — `apps/desktop/tests/permission-card-residue.test.ts` replays the exact run log from the report.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: a decided download no longer reappears as a disabled permission card when a Session is reopened; an approval-mode switch that clears pending requests also clears their cards.
Compatibility and migration: none. Existing event logs are read as before; the residue already in them is reconciled at read time and is not rewritten.

977.author: yuanzhou75
977.body:
Closes #954.

The remedy chosen in #954 is an explicit exclusion list (option "A" in the issue's Expected behavior): every `workspace_snapshot` re-hashes the whole tree on every turn, so a 470 MB `deps/` makes each turn cost 15–60 s. This PR makes `snapshotWorkspace` stop paying that cost for known generated/tooling directories — without trusting file metadata (the #641/#642 rule stands) and without silently producing a workspace that cannot be restored.

## What changes

- `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`
  - `TreeEntry` gains an `excluded` variant, so a skipped directory stays explicit in the tree instead of disappearing.
  - `snapshotWorkspace(store, root, options?)` accepts an `exclude` basename list (matched at any depth) and records each match as an `excluded` entry. The default is `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SNAPSHOT_EXCLUDE = ["deps", "node_modules", ".venv", "__pycache__"]`.
- `packages/cas/src/workspace-snapshot.ts`
  - `materializeWorkspaceSnapshot` now returns `{ excludedPaths }` and does not create excluded directories, so a fork/restore can report "these paths were excluded" instead of handing over a workspace that cannot run.

## Behavior

- Excluded directories are neither traversed nor stability-checked, so their per-file `open` / `hash` / `lstat` cost disappears from every turn (the reporter's 470 MB `deps/` becomes a single lstat).
- Nothing else changes: every non-excluded file is still re-hashed on each snapshot (metadata is never evidence), the whole-tree digest still covers the tree including the `excluded` markers, and a custom list can be passed. Wiring a per-workspace RuntimeSetting for the list is left as a follow-up; this PR defaults to the four known directories.

## Tests

- `versioning.test.ts`: a `deps/` directory is recorded as an `excluded` entry and its contents are skipped; `exclude` is configurable and `exclude: []` disables exclusion.
- `workspace-snapshot.test.ts`: a whole-tree export reports `["deps"]` in `excludedPaths` and materializes the rest.

Local pnpm test runs were not possible in this environment (no standalone Node/pnpm toolchain), so the CI merge-gate is the verification.

987.author: yuanzhou75
987.body:
## Summary

Fixes #978: a local Runner that answers a shell-execution submission with a definite 4xx (e.g. `401 "Execution not found for this Agent"`) previously left the tool call in an unconfirmed, never-settling state, so the run stayed in `running` forever.

This PR fixes the fallback side: a 4xx on submission proves the command never ran, so we now settle the execution as a committed `failed` record with a visible error, instead of downgrading it to an unknown/unconfirmed outcome.

## Root cause analysis

Two things were going on:

1. **Submission rejection was swallowed.** In `services/api/src/shell-executions.ts`, when the Runner rejected the submission with a 4xx, the `start()` catch branch only handled the "outcome unknown / unconfirmed" path (`unavailable(...)`). A definite 4xx was treated the same way, so the tool call never completed and the run stayed in `running` indefinitely.
2. **Idle timeout already works on latest `main`.** The issue's 25-minute-no-timeout observation was from `main @ bebd64e9`. On current `main`, the adapter's `stream_with_keepalive` sends blank-line keepalives while awaiting a tool (deliberately *without* resetting the run's own idle deadline), and the API-side `ndjson()` parser skips blank lines (`if (line)`), so idle timeout is armed and unaffected. No change needed there.

## Change

- Add `submissionRejected(error)` helper: true when `observationHttpStatus` is 400–499.
- In `start()`'s catch, when `!execution.accepted && submissionRejected(error)`, route to a new `rejectSubmission()` instead of `unavailable()`.
- `rejectSubmission()` maps the code:
  - `404` → `EXECUTION_NOT_FOUND`
  - `401`/`403` → `AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED`
  - otherwise → `SUBMISSION_REJECTED`
  and finishes the execution as `state: "failed", provenance: "committed"` with an error that states the command was not run, recording `lastError` as non-retryable.
- Added a unit test covering 401/404 submission rejections asserting the execution settles failed (not unknown).

The 401 root cause itself (why the Runner reports `Execution not found for this Agent`) is out of scope for this PR and tracked separately.

987.title: fix(agent): fail a shell execution whose submission the Runner rejected (closes #978)

988.author: yuanzhou75
988.body:
## Summary

Fixes #983: the research-copy integrity verifier falsely rejected a restored execution history whenever an execution ID had more than one observation.

Execution history is append-only by design — `appendExecutionRun` keeps an `unconfirmed` observation and appends the settled (`failed`/`succeeded`) observation under the same ID. The verifier selected the first row with that ID (`actual.find(item => item.id === ids.id(...))`), so every observation was compared against the first one. A `failed` observation (e.g. `environmentRevisionId: null`) was checked against the retained `unconfirmed` observation (e.g. `environmentRevisionId: "system-shell-bwrap-v1"`), producing the exact reported mismatch even when the history was restored correctly.

## Change

In `research-snapshot-integrity.ts`, for each of the execution-ish record kinds, group the target rows by ID and match each source row to the target row with the same ID at the same position (`(id, position)` pairing). The full record set is still verified: counts must be equal, every observation must have a paired restored twin, and all content/identity fields are compared as before.

Strict checks are preserved: a genuinely changed settled observation still fails (`executionRuns.status`), and a missing settled observation still fails (`executionRuns count`).

## Tests

Added to `research-snapshot-integrity.test.ts`:
- `unconfirmed → failed` and `unconfirmed → succeeded` duplicate observations restore and verify correctly.
- A changed settled observation still fails integrity.
- A missing settled observation still fails integrity.

This unblocks `export → delete source → import → create writable conversation → continue chat`; the root cause is independent of source deletion or the original environment catalog.

988.title: fix(api): match duplicate execution observations by order in research copy integrity (closes #983)

990.author: ink999107
990.body:
The literature journeys covered so far stop at the retrieval UI: they prove a search ran and a result list appeared, but not that a real model can turn live PubMed and bioRxiv evidence into a finished review. This adds one end-to-end real case that does.

## The journey

`test/literature-review-immune-liver-real.spec.ts` runs with every built-in specialist disabled, the Session detached from its specialist and Reviewer, an empty skill whitelist, and all installed literature MCP sources enabled. It submits one fixed question (adult versus pediatric liver parenchymal immune pathways, 2023-2025, top 14 enriched pathways, contradictions flagged) with delivery instructions that a machine can check, and then judges the handoff rather than the transcript:

- `literature_review.md` with `Methods`, `Results`, `Contradictory findings` and `References`; every section must carry content, the Methods must name the databases and the year range, and at least four distinct PMIDs/DOIs must be cited.
- `pathway_enrichment_counts.csv` with the exact header `pathway,adult_gene_count,pediatric_gene_count`, exactly 14 unique pathways and integer counts; both columns must contain a nonzero count, so an all-zero population column fails rather than passing as a degenerate chart.
- `pathway_enrichment_bar_chart.png` (or a documented `.svg` fallback) verified by its signature/size and by the adult/pediatric labels it renders.

A source that never returns records does not fail the case when the product reports it honestly: PubMed must return records and the review's Methods must name both PubMed and bioRxiv. A `BLOCKED:` precondition (literature source not ready, custom specialist present) marks the case blocked rather than failed.

## Why the bioRxiv assertion has this shape

`packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts` gives the bioRxiv `search_preprints` tool a trailing `days` window with a maximum of 365, so it cannot express a 2023-2025 range; during the local runs it returned either nothing or only 2026 preprints. Demanding a hit would make the case fail on a tool limitation, so it asserts that the search ran and that the review accounts for it in Methods.

## Validation

- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 6762, executed 6762, passed 6748, failed 14. All 14 are in untouched modules (launcher `serve`/`source-evolve`, `jiuwenswarm-agent`, `sandbox-network`, `start-stack-lock`, `bundled-references`); the same layer on unmodified `upstream/main` in a separate worktree reproduces the same failures, so they are pre-existing on this host. While collecting that baseline the run then stalled in `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` (`uv sync` against PyPI at 0% CPU), which is why the baseline summary file is incomplete.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 51, executed 51, passed 51, failed 0.
- `pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked browser subset): planned 136, executed 136, passed 132, failed 4, all in the `mocked-standard-config-global` shard (model connect wizard, provider catalog, custom MCP count, and `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)`). None of them load this spec, which is `@model:real` and excluded from the mocked project; the micromamba one is a host environment failure.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — real local stack, browser + API, on this branch's commit.

Case: `Literature review: adult vs pediatric liver immune pathways with a 14-pathway chart` (`@real @tier:l4`).

Command, per run:

```
CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 E2E_LLM_BASE_URL=… E2E_LLM_MODEL=… E2E_LLM_TOKEN=… \
E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1 CI_E2E_SPEC=test/literature-review-immune-liver-real.spec.ts \
CI_RESULTS_DIR=.e2e-results/runN bash .ci/run-e2e.sh real
```

Seven runs were made while settling the assertions; five passed. The two failures were in the test harness, not the product, and both were fixed before this commit:

- Run 2 failed on a bioRxiv record count that the tool cannot satisfy for a 2023-2025 question; the assertion is now "the search ran and Methods names both databases".
- Run 5 failed on `Results must report the comparison` because the spec's section extractor stopped at the first sub-heading; it now extends to the next heading of the same or higher level.

After both fixes, two consecutive runs passed:

| Run | Duration | PubMed | bioRxiv | Pathway rows | Nonzero adult / pediatric | Citations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | 13.8 min | 12 calls, 78 records | 4 calls, 2 records | 14 | 5 / 14 | 14 |
| 7 | 9.0 min | 3 calls, 30 records | 3 calls, 3 records | 14 | 7 / 12 | 34 |

Both runs declared all three artifacts, the chart rendered as PNG, and the reports carried all four sections.

## Summary

Fixes #985 (the selection-unaware IO half): `buildResearchPackageInput` collected workspace **payload bytes** before applying `selectedFiles` or necessary-export filtering, so a deselected large file still cost its full read, hash, and in-memory retention.

## Change

In `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts`:

- The per-session workspace pass now records only metadata (`path`, `size`, `modifiedAt`) and defers the read. A size preview still uses `addPreviewObject` (no bytes read); a real export leaves `objectPath` empty at first.
- After `selectedSessionRecords` is computed, a single pass reads each **retained** file's bytes once via `addObject`, fills its `objectPath`, and drops an unreadable file with an omission — matching the previous behavior where an unreadable file never entered the workspace list.
- A deselected file is therefore never read, hashed, or carried into `objects`. The later CAS/version dependency closure is unchanged, so evidence integrity is preserved.

## Scope

This is the collection-before-filter defect. Other reported cost paths (sequential CAS reads, trajectory hydration, revision validation, in-memory tar buffer) are noted in the issue as profile-then-attribute and are intentionally not claimed or changed here. Making the artifact-bearing workflow usable end-to-end also needs #983 (integrity), which is in progress.
991.head: fix-985-export-selection-before-io
991.title: fix(api): read retained workspace bytes only after export selection (closes #985)

992.body:
## Summary

Fixes the desktop half of #981: exporting a conversation could leave a persistent `legacy_unavailable` banner.

That string is the adapter's legacy proxy answering `502` with the internal code `legacy_unavailable` when the legacy API it forwards to is briefly unreachable. The desktop client surfaced that raw code as the error message, and the export poll retried it every three seconds with no bound, so the unexplained English code stayed on the page.

## Change

- `apps/desktop/src/api/client.ts`: add `isLegacyUnavailableError(reason)` (status 502 + message `legacy_unavailable`), mirroring `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`: the export poll now distinguishes outcomes:
  - `404` is terminal: the stale task is marked failed with a localized message (`exportMissing`).
  - `legacy_unavailable` is a transient service failure: show a localized `legacyUnavailable` retrying message, retry at the existing 3 s interval, and stop after 5 consecutive failures.
  - Other transient rejections retry a bounded 5 times, then show `exportPollingFailed`.
- `zh.ts` / `en.ts`: added `legacyUnavailable`, `exportPollingFailed`, `exportMissing`, localized in both languages.
- `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`: assert the 502 code is recognised and only for that code.

## Scope

This is the unclear-message + poll-churn half. The export/save interaction redesign and multi-task tracking are tracked separately in #986. The full root cause of *why* the legacy API was unreachable is not diagnosed here, per the issue's own note that this should be captured during reproduction rather than inferred.
992.head: fix-981-legacy-unavailable-message
992.title: fix(desktop): localise the adapter's legacy_unavailable error and stop its poll churn (closes #981)

993.author: yuanzhou75
993.body:
## Summary

Fixes #984: imported and research-copy sessions allocate a fresh executor session, so JiuwenSwarm — which holds and compresses its own per-session context — starts with no model-visible history. The restored transcript was displayed but never reached the model, so continuing an imported conversation lost the prior context (dialogue-only packages broke the central continuation promise).

## Change

Seed the restored history once, on the first continuation turn, as an equivalent model-context assembly:

- **`history-seed.ts`** folds the gateway history into a bounded, role-labelled block: `user:` / `assistant:` / `tool call:` / `tool result:` ordering is preserved, tool calls are named with their arguments, and a character budget keeps a large transcript from crowding out the turn (the opening user message is kept as an anchor).
- **`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`** prepends that block to the system prompt only when the run opts in via the new `seedModelContext` flag.
- **`runs/index.ts`** opts the run in when the session has an `imported_snapshot` / `research_copy` snapshot that has not been seeded yet, and marks `researchSnapshot.modelContextSeeded` once the first run completes — so subsequent turns, retries and restarts never duplicate the seed.
- **`packages/schema`** adds the `modelContextSeeded` marker; **`packages/workspace`** adds the `seedModelContext` option.

Native/specialist executors are unaffected: the flag is ignored by the native loop, which already assembles gateway history into its model context.

## Why this shape

JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6's `chat.send` contract has no history/messages field, and its session context lives only in-process (its own `warmup_session_context` reads its own `history.jsonl`, which SD's restored transcript never enters; there is no external history-write RPC). A cross-repo `history.seed` patch is the heavier alternative; this PR delivers the "equivalent model-context assembly" the issue allows, entirely on the SD side.

## Tests

- `history-seed.test.ts` covers role ordering/labelling, tool call/result recognition, budget bounding with the anchor, and empty/irrelevant-message handling.
- The issue's acceptance criteria (synthetic fact recall + first-model-request inspection, source present/deleted/clean destination, essential/full exports, no duplication on retry/restart, prefix-only branches inherit upstream) remain an end-to-end check I did not run here; the code path is unit-covered.
993.head: fix-984-model-context-seed
993.title: fix(agent): seed the restored conversation into JiuwenSwarm's model context (closes #984)

996.body:
A Project row keeps its `+` and `⋯` controls behind the fold's own name. The
toggle is a flex item, and a button's automatic minimum size is its content, so
a name longer than the column made the toggle lay out past the row instead of
shrinking. The controls were pushed outside the column, which clips horizontal
overflow, and became unreachable: neither hover nor keyboard focus nor the open
Project could reveal them. A Session row never had this problem because its
button already sets `min-width: 0`; the Project toggle was missing the same
line.

## The toggle can shrink

`.side-row.side-project .side-project-toggle` now carries `min-width: 0`.
Nothing else changes: the label's existing ellipsis starts working, so a long
name ends in `…` inside the row, and the existing hover, `:focus-within` and
active rules reveal `+` and `⋯` within the row's box instead of beyond it. The
full name stays in the button's tooltip, and double-click rename is unaffected.

## Captures

Taken with a throwaway spec in the mocked desktop suite — it uses the same
fixtures as the committed case and is not part of the diff — and cropped to the
sidebar. Each "before" pair was produced in a detached worktree at `main`
(`5033f026`), each "after" pair on this head. Both rows are hovered.

Sidebar width is 296px at a 1280px viewport and 256px at 1024px — the narrow
pair is the width where the failure bites hardest.

### zh-CN

| Wide (296px) — before, hovered | Wide (296px) — after, hovered |
| --- | --- |
| ![zh-CN before at 296px: the name runs past the clipped column, no controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/zh-CN/before-wide-hover.png) | ![zh-CN after at 296px: the name ends in an ellipsis and both controls sit inside the row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/zh-CN/after-wide-hover.png) |

| Narrow (256px) — before, hovered | Narrow (256px) — after, hovered |

Active/focused (`:focus-within`), 296px:

![zh-CN after, keyboard focus on the toggle: the focus ring is drawn and both controls are revealed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/zh-CN/after-wide-focused.png)

### en

| Wide (296px) — before, hovered | Wide (296px) — after, hovered |
| --- | --- |
| ![en before at 296px: the name runs past the clipped column, no controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/en/before-wide-hover.png) | ![en after at 296px: the name ends in an ellipsis and both controls sit inside the row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/en/after-wide-hover.png) |

In the "before" shots the name stops at the clipped edge with no `…` and the
row carries no controls at all, even while hovered; the chevron is pushed off
the row too. In the "after" shots the name ends in `…` and the chevron, `+` and
`⋯` all sit inside the row's right edge.

## Coverage

A mocked desktop e2e case renders a Project with a 72-character name and
asserts that the label computes `text-overflow: ellipsis` and has
`scrollWidth > clientWidth`, that both controls are hidden at rest, and that
hover brings them back inside the row's bounding box. Without the CSS line the
case fails at the truncation assertion, so the regression is caught rather than
described.

## Validation

Run on commit 58a78978.

- Desktop package unit tests (`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`):
  821 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Desktop mocked e2e (`apps/desktop/e2e/projects.spec.ts`): 4 passed, 0 failed.
- UT layer (`pnpm ci:ut`): planned 6587, executed 6558, passed 6545, failed 13,
  skipped 0. All 13 failures reproduce with identical counts on unmodified
  `main` (5033f026) in a separate detached worktree, so none is introduced by
  this change. They are host conditions:
  - `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` (5) and
    `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts` (5): a stray
    `/tmp/package.json` outside the repository declares `"type": "module"`, so
    the CommonJS `dist/server.js` the launcher spawns is treated as ESM.
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` (1): the trajectory
    database cannot be opened in this host's temporary directory.
  - `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` (1): the host bubblewrap
    rejects `--disable-userns`, an option the sandbox test passes.
  - `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs` (1): the interrupt simulation restores
    its mirror on this host instead of reproducing the interrupted write.
- ST layer (`pnpm ci:st`): planned 51, executed 51, passed 49, failed 2. Both
  failures are local provisioning, not the change: the JiuwenSwarm SDK check
  could not install `chromadb` because the run was pinned offline against a
  cache that predates it, and the Evolve distribution journey downloads the
  pinned Python runtime and source from the network, which the same offline
  run blocked.

### CI on this head

Two runs so far, both red for the same reason: GitHub's release download host
answers `504`.

- Run `42466721872` (first run) and run `42469129753` (after closing and
  reopening the pull request): `ST` reports 50 of 51 passed, 1 failed — the
  single failure is `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts`, which fetches the
  pinned runtime and dies with
  `Download failed (504): https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz`
  (quoted from the `st-results` artifact of that run).
- In the second run three mocked shards — `governed`, `research`,
  `standard-config` — failed before reaching a test: `astral-sh/setup-uv@v6`
  logged `Unexpected HTTP response: 504` three times in each job and gave up.
- `merge-gate` is red because those jobs are red; it runs nothing of its own
  that this diff touches.
- The rest of the run is green: `L1`, `UT`, `Coverage`,
  `CodeCheck (GitCode)`, and the `literature` and `standard-journeys` mocked
  shards. The 13 UT failures listed above are this host's, not CI's.

The same `ST` job did pass on `main` at `239dde7d` (run `42465227603`), which
is the reviewer's point — but that run is itself red for the same infra reason:
`L2 E2E (mocked, research)` and `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` both died
with `Unexpected HTTP response: 504`, and `merge-gate` followed, while `ST`
happened to get through. So the trunk and this head are failing against a
download host that is answering `504`, not against each other. This diff
touches `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` and
`apps/desktop/e2e/projects.spec.ts` only. Once the host recovers the run is
re-triggered; a fresh result will be posted here.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — local, mocked, tested commit 58a78978 on
`fix/desktop-long-project-name`. Browser: desktop Chromium via
`apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts`.

- A Project with a 72-character name → the name is ellipsized inside the row,
  both controls are hidden at rest, and hovering reveals `+` and `⋯` inside
  the row → PASS.
- Existing Project journeys in the same spec (rename through a reload, delete
  with confirmation, delete the Project of the open Session) → PASS.

Totals: 4 passed / 0 failed / 0 blocked / 0 skipped.

**The desktop shell is deliberately out of CI.** `apps/desktop/e2e` is not
referenced by any workflow in `.github/workflows` or `.ci`; the mocked matrix
drives `apps/web`, which needs the Python control plane, and its fixture puts a
project, a token and a model in place before a spec starts — the opposite of a
desktop journey, which has to begin from an empty workspace. Keeping the suite
local is the design, not an oversight, so this evidence is reported as local
rather than as a CI gate. Wiring the desktop shell into the matrix would be its
own change.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
GitHub label: `release:fix` is pending a maintainer — this fork has no write
access to apply labels, so the category is stated here instead.
User impact: A Project whose name does not fit the column now shows a
truncated name with `…` and keeps its `+` (new session in the Project) and `⋯`
(rename/delete) controls reachable on hover, keyboard focus or when the
Project is active.
Compatibility and migration: none.

999.author: yuanzhou75
999.body:
Fixes #986

## What changed

### Desktop shell (`win_desktop`)
- New export IPC: a native "save as" dialog that remembers the last chosen directory and asks before overwriting (`sd-shell:export-save-dialog`), a destination-bound file write (`sd-shell:export-write`), open-file-location (`sd-shell:export-show-in-folder`) and the OS downloads dir (`sd-shell:export-downloads-dir`).
- The renderer only writes into the path the user picked in the native dialog — no unrestricted filesystem access from the renderer.
- Exposed as `window.sdShell.exportFile` in the preload; `lastExportDir` is persisted (`export-state.json`) so the next export defaults to the last used folder.

### Desktop export flow (`apps/desktop`)
- **Choose the destination first**: confirming export opens the native save dialog (default name `会话标题_YYYYMMDD_HHmm.sdresearch`, default folder = last used folder, else the OS downloads folder). Cancelling the dialog aborts the export without starting a packaging task.
- **Automatic save**: once packaging completes, the archive is written to the chosen destination automatically — no second Download click.
- **Independent exports**: each export keeps its own task id, destination and result; starting a second export no longer overwrites the first's tracking.
- **Unobtrusive feedback**: small bottom-page text shows "N exports in progress" (expandable, each task cancellable); a green/red completion flash appears for a few seconds and disappears, with an "open file location" action.
- The export dialog keeps a persistent "saved packages" list with open-location and retry-save (a save failure reuses the already-generated archive rather than repackaging).

### API
- `POST /api/projects/{id}/research-package/exports/{task}/cancel` plus a `canceled` terminal state; cancelling during packaging drops the produced archive.

### Browser fallback
In a plain browser (no Electron shell) there is no pre-packaging native save dialog; the supported equivalent is a browser download after packaging completes, via the browser's own save prompt, keeping the same automatic-save-on-completion behaviour.

## Tests
- `win_desktop/test/export-state.test.ts`: last-directory persistence.
- `services/api/src/research-package-exports.test.ts`: cancelled queued/running exports never produce a download.
- `apps/desktop/tests/research-package.test.ts`: cancel + archive-blob client coverage.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/research-package.spec.ts`: updated for automatic save and completion feedback.

## Screenshots
UI change — screenshots to be attached after a desktop build is available.
